_comment: All limits live here so you can tune risk without touching code. Re-read every cycle.
_a_skip_comment: Extra layer 'A-skip': sleeve A's minute-4 rule on the weaker signals A skips (1.0 <= |z| < 1.5), own $100 ledger (stops if it is used up), $10 flat stake per bet (extra_stake_dollars below), at most 50% of its ledger open at once. Set false to switch it off.
_c_loose_comment: Extra layer 'C-loose' (loose paper bot's C: minute 11 at 1.5 sigma, $100 tier) on a dedicated $40 ledger, bets at most 50% of that ledger at once, never draws more from the main balance, no 1-contract minimum. Set false to switch it off.
_size_multiplier_comment: Fallback tier multiplier only when percentage sizing and flat sizing are disabled. Percentage sizing is currently active.
_flat_stake_dollars_comment: When set, every sleeve bets this many flat dollars whenever it fires. Overridden by stake_pct_of_balance below when that is also set. Set both to null to go back to the paper bot's original tiered sizes (A/D/E $40, B/C/F $100) times size_multiplier.
_safe_mode_comment: Price cap is OFF so the entry logic matches the original paper bot (only the 3-97 cent band applies). To re-enable a cap set e.g. 0.93. Backups: config.json.bak_before_safemode.
_total_stake_pct_of_balance_comment: Normal sizing: share 30% of tradeable equity (less the dedicated extra ledger) among firing standard sleeves in their original 40:100 weights, as on Oct 12. Each sleeve's share is then scaled by sleeve_throttle.
_addon_stake_pct_of_available_comment: Per explicit request: once a position is already open on a ticker+rule and the signal is STILL firing (same z-score/rule check as the original entry), if the price for that side has gotten CHEAPER than the position's own average entry cost, add to it ONCE -- allocate this fraction of currently-available free liquid cash (the same shard-scoped spendable balance used for sizing, not total equity), split across every sleeve eligible for this rule proportionally to their original relative weight, same as total_stake_pct_of_balance. Only ever fires once per position (flagged via pos['addon_done']), not every time price ticks cheaper again, and never if the original signal has stopped firing. Set to 0 or null to disable add-ons entirely.
_demo_note: There is deliberately no 'demo' config field. Whether the bot can touch real money is controlled ONLY by the --demo CLI flag plus the KALSHI_LIVE=1 and --live gates -- never by something editable in a config file the bot re-reads automatically while already running.
_max_total_open_pct_comment: Aggregate open-exposure ceiling: 90% of tradeable account equity across all sleeves, as on Oct 12.
_max_market_open_dollars_comment: Hard ceiling: no more than this many dollars open in any single market (all sleeves combined), regardless of sleeve caps. Raised to fit up to 5-6 sleeves each betting flat_stake_dollars on the same contract.
_max_orders_per_cycle_comment: Hard ceiling on how many new orders the bot will place in one ~15s loop iteration, in case many coins signal at once.
_max_order_size_dollars_comment: Hard ceiling on the dollar size of any single combined order, after sleeves are merged. Raised to match max_market_open_dollars.
_daily_loss_limit_comment: Disabled per explicit request (removed, not just raised -- set absurdly high so the check is permanently a no-op rather than deleting the code path). No daily stop-trading circuit breaker exists anymore: the bot will keep placing new orders regardless of today's realized losses. All other limits (max_total_open_pct, max_market_open_dollars, max_order_size_dollars, each sleeve's 50% cap) are unaffected and still apply.
_stale_feed_comment: If a coin's Coinbase candle has not advanced in this many seconds, that coin is treated as having a stale feed and skipped; repeated staleness across the board halts the bot.
_cycle_interval_comment: 4s between cycles (~6-7s per full cycle) so each coin gets 4-5 checks inside every 30-second decision window. At 12s (~15s cycles) live only got 2 checks and missed paper's XRP 10:00 min-11 bet on Oct 19 by reaching it at minute 11.44 when the price was already over 97c. 4s was verified rate-limit safe earlier.
_max_consecutive_errors_comment: Halt the whole bot after this many API errors in a row (across any series, within one cycle's loop). Previously hardcoded in the Python; moved here so it's visible and tunable.
_max_stale_strikes_comment: Halt only if EVERY coin's feed is stale for this many cycles in a row. 8 at the 4s interval (~7s cycles) is ~50s, the same wall-clock tolerance as 3 at the old 12s interval; 3 at 4s halted on normal Coinbase candle-publish lag (Oct 19).
_settlement_grace_comment: reconcile() tolerates a tracked position missing from the exchange's unsettled-positions view for up to this long after its market closes (confirmed live: a market can drop out of 'unsettled' slightly before its public result is queryable) before treating it as a genuine mismatch instead of normal settlement lag. Previously hardcoded at 600s (10 min).
_close_safety_margin_comment: A still-resting order is cancelled this many seconds before its market actually closes, rather than waiting until the literal close instant, so the cancel has time to process. Previously hardcoded.
_reconciliation_tolerance_comment: reconcile() only halts if the bot's tracked position differs from the exchange's real position by more than this many contracts -- a small cushion for float rounding, not meant to mask a real mismatch (a genuine error is almost always a whole contract or more off). Previously hardcoded. Raised from 0.5 to 1.0 on 2026-10-17 after a crash loop: a min_one_contract (1-contract) order partially filled at 0.73 contracts, got truncated to 0 by _truncate_fractional_count, and the resulting 0.73 gap could never close (truncation always rounds down, no further fill was coming) -- it exceeded the old 0.5 tolerance on every retry, exhausted max_halt_retries, and because halt_retries persists in saved state across restarts, every subsequent restart hit the SAME exceeded-retries path immediately, with no retry window at all. 1.0 still can't mask a genuine whole-contract-or-more error per the note above.
_sleeve_fixed_stake_dollars_comment: Empty so every sleeve uses its share of total_stake_pct_of_balance (Oct 12 sizing). Previous targets were A $100, B $50; see config.json.bak_before_throttle.
_sleeve_throttle_comment: Per-sleeve brake: a sleeve's realized loss over the last window_hours, as a share of account balance, cuts that sleeve's stake AND its open-bet cap. Lost 5%+ -> half size, 10%+ -> quarter, 15%+ -> 10%. Recovers on its own as losses age out of the window or wins offset them. Changes are logged as sleeve_throttle events.
_exposure_room_divisor_comment: Each signal's total stake is capped at room/3, where room = max_total_open_pct x balance minus what is already open. A lone signal still gets the full 30%; when many coins fire at once later ones get smaller bets instead of being skipped, so live fires every bet the original paper bot fires. Remove to go back to skipping.
_blocked_hours_comment: Empty for parity with the original paper bot (which has no hour block). Was [3, 7] with blocked_hours_min_sigma 2.5; see config.json.bak_before_parity2.
_combo_new_comment: After each rule's 30s window, combo-new buys ONE $50 Kalshi combo of every leg A-F actually hold for that window (2+ legs), via RFQ, on the combo shard (exchange_index 1 -- needs cash THERE, not on the crypto shard). Accepts the cheapest quote only if its YES price is within [fair-0.05, fair+0.15] (fair = product of leg prices) and <= 0.95; verifies a YES position after, else disables itself. mode 'quote_only' requests quotes but never buys. enabled false turns it off. Records: combo_state.json, combo_history.jsonl.
_combo_new_mode_comment: paper_test: driven by the ORIGINAL PAPER bot's bets; requests a real $50 quote, never accepts, records a paper combo at the quoted price, settles it on the combo's real result, then switches mode to 'live' by itself. live: real $50 combos from live A-F legs. quote_only: quotes from live legs, never buys.
_stale_comment: A coin is skipped only if its Coinbase 1-minute candle hasn't advanced in 300s. Was 60s, but thin coins (HYPE, BNB, ZEC) often go 1-2 minutes with no trades, so no new candle; that made live skip bets the original paper bot (which has no stale check) took -- e.g. HYPE 18:15 min-4 on Oct 19. The all-coins-stale halt still applies.
